info.name: LightingFX
info.comment: Enables the application of lighting effects.

description.p: The lighting effect class applies a diffuse or specular lighting effect to the alpha channel of an input bitmap, which functions as a bump map. The output is an RGBA representation of the light effect. If no light Colour is specified by the client then the output will be in grey scale.
For diffuse lighting, the resulting RGBA image is computed as follows:
description.pre: Dr = kd * N.L * Lr Dg = kd * N.L * Lg Db = kd * N.L * Lb Da = 1.0
description.p: where
description.pre: kd = Diffuse lighting constant N = Surface normal unit vector, a function of x and y L = Unit vector pointing from surface to light, a function of x and y in the point and spot light cases Lr,Lg,Lb = RGB components of light, a function of x and y in the spot light case
description.p: For specular lighting, the resulting RGBA image is computed as follows:
description.pre: Sr = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lr Sg = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lg Sb = ks * pow(N.H, specularExponent) * Lb Sa = max(Sr, Sg, Sb)
description.p: where
description.pre:
ks = Specular lighting constant N = Surface normal unit vector, a function of x and y H = "Halfway" unit vector between eye unit vector and light unit vector
Lr,Lg,Lb = RGB components of light
description.p: The definition of H reflects our assumption of the constant eye vector E = (0,0,1):
where L is the light unit vector.

The light is computed in the colour space of the parent VectorFilter. In SRGB the light Colour and the result are sRGB values. In LINEAR_RGB the light Colour is converted to linear RGB and the result is encoded to sRGB for storage, so a result of 0.5 is stored as approximately 0.735.

The SVG algorithm measures the slope of the bump map with a 3x3 kernel. This softens fine detail and shows 8-bit steps on gentle slopes. When the VectorScene.Compliance of the scene is NONE (the default), the enhancements selected by the Features field are applied. All of them are enabled by default:

list.li: DEQUANTISE: Heights are read as floating point values, and areas that vary by no more than one alpha level are smoothed to remove terracing.
SHARPEN: Slopes are measured with a sharper gradient, which keeps more of the detail in features a few pixels wide.
CAVITY: Narrow creases and pits receive less light, in proportion to their curvature.
DETAIL: Fine detail is given more relief than broad shapes, so that it remains visible at a surface scale that suits the larger forms.

SHADOWS: Distant lights cast shadows. A point is unlit when the surface between it and the light rises above the light's elevation, and the edge of the shadow softens with distance from the surface that casts it.
SPECULAR_AA: Specular highlights are widened where the surface varies within a pixel, so that high exponents do not produce isolated bright pixels.

description.p: Flat surfaces and broad shapes are lit the same as the SVG algorithm, but shadows can darken any surface that lies beside a raised area. Set the scene's Compliance to SVG1 or SVG2 for results that match the SVG specification exactly, or set Features to zero to use the SVG algorithm for this effect alone.

method.name: SetDistantLight
method.comment: Configure lighting with a distant light source.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetDistantLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE Azimuth, DOUBLE Elevation)

input.param: Direction angle for the light source on the XY plane (clockwise), in degrees from the X axis.
Direction angle for the light source from the XY plane towards the Z axis, in degrees. A positive value points towards the viewer of the content.

description.p: This method applies a distant light configuration to the lighting effect. It will override any previously defined light source setting.

A distant light can be thought of as like the light from the sun. An infinite amount of parallel light rays travel in the direction that the distant light points to. Distant lights are handy when you want equal illumination on objects in a scene.

method.name: SetPointLight
method.comment: Configure lighting with a pointed light source.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetPointLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Z)

input.param: X location for the light source.
Y location for the light source.
Z location for the light source.

description.p: This method applies a pointed light configuration to the lighting effect. It will override any previously defined light source setting.

A point light sends light out from the specified (X, Y, Z) location equally in all directions. A light bulb or open flame is a good example of a point light. The intensity of the light can be controlled by altering the alpha component of the light Colour.

method.name: SetSpotLight
method.comment: Configure lighting with a spot light source.
method.prototype: ERR lt::SetSpotLight(OBJECTPTR Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Z, DOUBLE PX, DOUBLE PY, DOUBLE PZ, DOUBLE Exponent, DOUBLE ConeAngle)

input.param: X location for the light source.
Y location for the light source.
Z location for the light source. The positive Z-axis comes out towards the person viewing the content and assuming that one unit along the Z-axis equals one unit in X and Y.
X location of the light source's target.
Y location of the light source's target.
Z location of the light source's target.
Exponent value controlling the focus for the light source.
A limiting cone which restricts the region where the light is projected, or 0 to disable. Specified in degrees.

description.p: This method applies a spot light configuration to the lighting effect. It will override any previously defined light source setting.
A spot light beams light rays from the defined (X, Y, Z) position to the (PX, PY, PZ) position. The Exponent and ConeAngle work together to constrain the edge of the light projection.

field.name: Colour
field.comment: Defines the colour of the light source.

description.p: Set the Colour field to define the colour of the light source.
If the algorithm supports it, the Alpha component defines the intensity of the light source.
The default colour is pure white.

field.name: Constant
field.comment: Specifies the ks/kd value in Phong lighting model.

description.p: In the Phong lighting model, this field specifies the kd value in diffuse mode, or ks value in specular mode.

field.name: Exponent
field.comment: Exponent for specular lighting, larger is more "shiny". Ranges from 1.0 to 128.0.

description.p: This field defines the exponent value for specular lighting, within a range of 1.0 to 128.0. The larger the value, shinier the end result.

field.name: Features
field.comment: Selects the enhancements applied to the SVG lighting algorithm.

description.p: When the VectorScene.Compliance of the scene is NONE, the lighting algorithm is extended with the features enabled here. The default is ALL. Each feature can be disabled independently, for instance to remove shadows from content that is lit from a low angle, or to tune the appearance of an effect that was designed for the SVG algorithm. Disabling SHARPEN measures slopes with the same kernel as the SVG algorithm.
If no features are enabled, the SVG algorithm is used without modification. Features have no effect when the Compliance of the scene is SVG1 or SVG2.

field.name: Scale
field.comment: The maximum height of the input surface (bump map) when the alpha input is 1.0.

description.p: The height is measured in kernel units when computing the surface normal, so the steepness of the lit surface is determined by Scale in combination with UnitX and UnitY. Refer to UnitX for details.

field.name: Type
field.comment: Defines the type of surface light scattering, which can be specular or diffuse.

field.name: UnitX
field.comment: The intended distance in current filter units for dx in the surface normal calculation formulas.

description.p: Indicates the intended distance in current filter units (i.e. as determined by the value of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits) for dx in the surface normal calculation formulas. This is equivalent to the first value of the SVG kernelUnitLength attribute.

If UnitX is not specified, the kernel unit is one unit of the client vector's coordinate system, regardless of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits. The appearance of the lighting then depends on the size of the bump map in those units: the same graphic will look flatter when it is drawn larger in its own coordinate system, but not when it is magnified by a parent transform.

By specifying UnitX in bounding box units, the kernel becomes relative to the filter's bounds, which are measured on the same terms as BlurFX. A bump map that is blurred and lit in bounding box units will then have the same appearance at any size and display resolution.
The value must be greater than zero. Rather than resampling the bump map to the kernel grid, the surface gradient is measured per pixel and scaled to the kernel unit.

field.name: UnitY
field.comment: The intended distance in current filter units for dy in the surface normal calculation formulas.

description.p: Indicates the intended distance in current filter units (i.e. as determined by the value of VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits) for dy in the surface normal calculation formulas. This is equivalent to the second value of the SVG kernelUnitLength attribute. The value must be greater than zero. Refer to UnitX for further details.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Returns an SVG compliant XML string that describes the filter.

constants.comment: Enhanced lighting features for the LightingFX class. These apply only when the scene's Compliance is `NONE`.
constants.const: Synonym for DEQUANTISE | SHARPEN | CAVITY | DETAIL | SHADOWS | SPECULAR_AA
Darken narrow creases and pits in proportion to their curvature.
Smooth areas that vary by no more than one alpha level, removing the terraces of 8-bit heights.
Give fine detail more relief than broad shapes.
Distant lights cast shadows from raised areas of the surface.
Measure slopes with a 4th-order gradient that keeps more of the detail in narrow features. If not set, the SVG Sobel kernel is used.
Widen specular highlights where the surface varies within a pixel, preventing sparkle at high exponents.

constants.comment: Lighting algorithm for the LightingFX class.
